title: Insights into why cybersecurity and resilience are at the top of the executive agenda
summary: Insights into why cybersecurity and resilience are at the top of the executive agenda A dynamic and dangerous landscape Insights from across the globe The importance of threat avoidance
body_text: Insights into why cybersecurity and resilience are at the top of the executive agenda A dynamic and dangerous landscape Insights from across the globe The importance of threat avoidance Available to engage with you and your teams A dynamic and dangerous landscape Over the last 18 months, in the U.S. alone, we have witnessed cybersecurity breaches of everything from the U.S. Treasury to our trial courts. America’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) was itself compromised. The University of Maryland reports that a cyber breach occurs on average every 39 seconds. In addition to dozens of compromises of major corporations and public entities, whether through systems or supply chains, this last year has seen vulnerabilities tied to the largest global technology firms , core security firms , and a range of software and service providers . These risks are compounded by the rise and rapid proliferation of cloud services (with their attendant “shared fate” and responsibility models), remote software as a service (SaaS) platforms , extended third-party provider networks (subject to lowest common denominator vulnerabilities) and, of course, artificial intelligence —where we have seen AI “leaks” and exposures in solutions ranging from chatbots to LLMs. Amid this remarkable, now often AI-fueled barrage, cybersecurity experts rightly advise that we “assume constant breach.” Insights from across the globe It is with this emerging and dynamic threat landscape in mind that I digested with interest findings from the 2025 Voice of Our Clients , in which we synthesize direct feedback from more than 1,800 business and IT executives worldwide. I engaged in a handful of these conversations, interviewing CIOs and business leaders in education, retail, and manufacturing. Cybersecurity , data protection and risk management ranked within the top 5 areas of importance across global industry trends and business and IT priorities. Indeed, respondents this year characterized security and compliance as drivers of their core modernization work , which makes sense given the risks to businesses represented by mounting technical debt. 85% of executives interviewed suggested they are weighing cybersecurity risks heavily when entrusting work to external partners and consultancies; and virtually all addressed the need for strengthening supply chain and ecosystem resilience, efficiency, and security. Across industries, cybersecurity and data protection command substantial mindshare and investment even as AI dominates the news cycle. No company or public entity wants to be next in the pantheon of cyber breaches. It is especially instructive to examine responses from those who are producing expected results from their digital strategies—we categorize these executives as the “digital leaders.” We found that digital leaders in manufacturing rely on mature industry security frameworks. In energy and utilities, digital leaders prioritize data, workforce, and security readiness—also leveraging AI, cybersecurity and modernization to deliver value, stay compliant, and reinforce their supply chains. In the public sector, particularly among federal and central government respondents, we see that securing legacy systems and maintaining cyber vigilance in a geopolitical environment is critical to safeguarding sensitive data, addressing evolving threats (including from nation state actors) and sustaining citizen confidence in digital services. Communications firms are becoming next-gen digital service providers, weaving network security into their value-added services, ranging from identity management and privilege consent to encryption and firewalls. The importance of threat avoidance Around the world, we actively are securing clients’ internal and externally facing systems and infrastructure, whether we are collaborating with nuclear facilities, municipal systems, or manufacturers’ Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT). We recognize that cybersecurity attacks are increasingly sophisticated. Data breaches cost companies millions. Risks are, if anything, commoditized; AI represents a growing attack vector, with workloads subject to critical vulnerabilities; and identity-based attacks are on the rise. While the global cyber threat landscape is both “dangerous and complex,” many of the most effective responses are deceptively simple, amounting to basic security hygiene in patching and attention to the fundamentals. Lapses all too often arise from human error (which Gartner suggested was at the root of 99% of firewall breaches in 2023). This includes: use of default passwords weak credentials data oversharing default cloud and service account configurations, often with elevated permissions. We have seen gaps in readiness: inadequate access controls , absence of multi-factor authentication , neglect of authentication logs . Companies face misconfigurations in everything from firewalls to blob storage containers—cloud systems accidentally being set to public instead of private, for example—not to mention predictable prevalence of human susceptibility to phishing, vishing, and more. In my own conversations with clients, I spend a lot of time bringing forward lessons learned and best practices from our work with organizations in the U.S. and across our global operations. We advise both public and private sector clients on AI guardrails and mechanisms to protect against breaches and intrusions. And we offer 24 by 7 monitoring and security operations services every day of the year for public entities and businesses ranging from mid-market companies to global powerhouses. Available to engage with you and your teams We deliver a range of advisory and operations services tied to ensuring and protecting trusted digital identities, effectively managing digital risks, building modern, proactive digital security operations, and operating and transforming securely with pace and confidence (including via hyper-automation and DevSecOps). Our cybersecurity capabilities align with key needs across industries and can be adapted to the specifics of each client’s maturity, environment, and challenges. I am happy to engage locally or to guide you to my colleagues in your geography to explore how we can help you meet today’s cybersecurity challenges and those on the horizon. Back to top

title: 10 Best Face Serums for Women
summary: Upgrade your skincare routine with the best face serums for women. Discover top picks for hydration, glowing skin, dark spots, acne, and anti-aging.
body_text: Why Use Face Serums? Benefits of Face Serums 10 Face Serums for Women Right Serum for Your Skin Types of Face Serums Steps to Apply Face Serum Mistakes While Using Serums FAQs Skincare shelves today are overflowing with promises, but only a handful of products actually deliver visible change and face serums are one of them. Light and easily absorbed face serums with active ingredients are now an essential part of any skincare routine due to their effective results. From achieving radiant skin to lightening dark marks or a smoother, even texture the perfect face serums can provide real results within weeks. With numerous face serums from different brands promising to be the best for your skin, how do you know which one will suit your skin? This is exactly what we will be discussing in this guide. We've rounded up the best face serum for women options available today considering some important factors like ingredient quality, skin type suitability, concentration of actives, and real-world results. Apart from this, you will also learn how to select a face serum for women depending on your skin needs, what kind of serums are available in the market, and how to properly use them. By the end, you'll have everything you need to pick a face serum for women that truly works for you. Why Face Serums Are Essential for Healthy Skin? Serums are made with a higher percentage of active ingredients compared to moisturizers and lotions. It means that serums will absorb deeply into the skin and target specific concerns more effectively. Unlike bulkier products, serums have a light consistency, fast-absorbing texture that delivers ingredients such as vitamin C, niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, and retinol directly where they are required. This makes them ideal for addressing issues such as dullness, uneven skin tone, acne marks, or even early signs of aging. Using high-quality serums regularly is capable of providing noticeable results in skin clarity, hydration, and overall texture over time. They also act as a supportive layer between cleansing and moisturizing, enhancing the effectiveness of the rest of your routine. For anyone looking to build an effective skincare routine the inclusion of a serum isn't just an add-on step it's often the difference between skin that simply looks okay and skin that genuinely glows. That's why serums have become a never skipped step in most skincare enthusiasts today. Benefits of Using a Face Serum The best face serum for women not only acts on the outer layer but also takes care of multiple issues of the skin. Here are the results you will get from using serums on a regular basis: Deep hydration: Serums with hyaluronic acid draw moisture into the skin keeping it plump, soft, and hydrated throughout the day. Brighter complexion: Serums containing vitamin C and niacinamide give your face a bright, healthy and radiant glow. Fades pigmentation: Targeted actives will degrade excess melanin and help reduce the appearance of dark spots. Reduces acne marks: Ingredients like niacinamide and salicylic acid will be helpful to improve skin tone. Controls excess oil: Lightweight oil-controlling serums will balance sebum production. Improves skin texture: Regular application of such products helps to even out skin texture and to make it softer. Supports collagen production: Peptide and vitamin C serums stimulate collagen synthesis to keep skin firm and youthful. Reduces fine lines and wrinkles: Anti-aging serums with retinol or peptides help soften expression lines and delay visible aging. How to Choose the Best Face Serum for Your Skin Type Not every serum works for every skin type, so understanding your skin type is the first step toward picking the right formula. Here's a quick breakdown to help you decide. For Dry Skin Go for serums that contain ingredients such as hyaluronic acid, glycerin, or ceramides, which will ensure the skin is well hydrated. Hydrating serums restore skin softness, prevent flakiness, and leave the skin moisturized all day without being greasy or heavy on the skin. For Oily Skin Use lighter serums with ingredients such as niacinamide or salicylic acid to regulate sebum production and prevent oily skin. Light serums with niacinamide or salicylic acid are quick-absorbing and will help in controlling acne while refining pores. For Combination Skin Go for serums that are balanced and have either niacinamide or lightweight hydrators that address both oily and dry zones simultaneously. The formula will hydrate the dry areas, such as cheeks while controlling oil in the T-zone, creating a more even, balanced complexion overall. For Sensitive Skin Use products that are free of fragrances and contain soothing agents, like centella asiatica or panthenol , to prevent any kind of irritation. They help soothe the skin, build up the skin barrier, and make the skin less reactive. For Acne-Prone Skin Choose serums that contain salicylic acid, niacinamide, or tea tree extract to manage breakouts and control oiliness. They work by decongesting pores, decreasing inflammation and healing acne scars without drying out the skin further. For Mature Skin Use serums that are rich in retinol, peptides, or vitamin C to address wrinkles, sagging, and lack of firmness. They work by stimulating collagen production and restoring elasticity to the skin. Types of Face Serums Every Woman Should Know Beyond skin type, serums are also categorized by the specific concern they target. Knowing these categories makes it easier to build a routine that actually addresses your skin goals. Hydrating Face Serums The serums in this category usually include ingredients like hyaluronic acid or glycerin that act as moisturizers, attracting moisture into the skin. This kind of serum works great for dry skin and gives an instant plumping effect to the skin. Brightening Face Serums These types of serums are combined with vitamin C or extracts from licorice root to brighten skin and even out skin tone. Regular use helps fade dark spots, boosts radiance, and gives the complexion a healthier, more luminous appearance overall. Anti-Aging Face Serums Combining active ingredients such as retinol or peptides, these serums address wrinkles and signs of aging such as fine lines and sagging skin. They stimulate collagen production and improve elasticity, helping skin look visibly smoother and more youthful with consistent use. Acne-Fighting Face Serums Such serums are made with salicylic acid, niacinamide, or tea tree oil that work towards getting rid of breakouts and regulate excessive oils. They unclog pores, reduce inflammation, and prevent acne, as well as heal any blemishes. Dark Spot & Pigmentation Face Serums Serums containing active ingredients such as alpha arbutin or kojic acid will be able to target the formation of melanin that helps in lightening any hyperpigmented skin spots or marks. Barrier Repair Face Serums These serums include ceramides and fatty acids, which enhance the skin's natural protective barrier. These serums are perfect for compromised, sensitive, or over-exfoliated skin. It makes the skin stronger and prevents dehydration in the long run. Exfoliating Face Serums These serums have alpha hydroxy acids or beta hydroxy acids such as glycolic or salicylic acid. They help remove dead skin cells from the skin surface, making it soft and glowing. Soothing Face Serums for Sensitive Skin Formulated with centella asiatica, aloe vera, or panthenol, these serums calm redness and irritation instantly. They're gentle enough for daily use, helping sensitive skin feel more comfortable and less reactive over time. Tips to Apply Face Serum the Right Way Even the best face serum for women won't deliver results if it isn't applied correctly. Follow these simple tips to get the most out of every drop. Start with clean skin: Always apply serum on freshly cleansed and toned skin so the active ingredients can absorb properly without any barrier of dirt or oil in the way. Use the right amount: A few drops are usually enough. Applying too much serum doesn't speed up results and can sometimes overwhelm the skin, especially with potent actives like vitamin C or retinol. Apply on damp skin: Applying serum to slightly damp skin helps lock in extra moisture and improves absorption, making the product work more effectively than on completely dry skin. Pat, don't rub: Gently pat the serum into your skin using your fingertips instead of rubbing it in harshly, which helps with better absorption and prevents unnecessary friction or irritation. Follow with moisturizer: Always seal in your serum with a suitable moisturizer to lock in hydration and active ingredients, preventing them from evaporating off the skin's surface. Don't forget SPF: If you're using an active serum during the day, especially vitamin C or exfoliating acids, always follow up with sunscreen to protect your skin from sun damage. Common Mistakes to Avoid When Using Face Serums Small application errors can reduce the effectiveness of even the best face serum for glowing skin for women. Here are some common mistakes to watch out for. Skipping patch tests: Introducing a new serum without patch testing can lead to unexpected irritation, especially with strong actives like retinol or high-percentage vitamin C formulas. Mixing incompatible actives: Combining ingredients like retinol and vitamin C, or multiple exfoliating acids, in the same routine can irritate skin instead of improving it, so layer actives carefully. Using too many serums at once: Layering multiple serums with different actives can overwhelm the skin barrier and reduce overall effectiveness, so it's best to keep your routine simple and targeted. Expecting overnight results: Serums need consistent use over several weeks to show visible results, so patience and regularity matter more than switching products too soon. Ignoring skin type: Using a serum that doesn't match your skin type or concern, like a heavy hydrating serum on very oily skin, can lead to disappointing or counterproductive results. Skipping sunscreen: Many active ingredients, especially exfoliants and vitamin C, increase sun sensitivity, so skipping SPF afterward can undo all the benefits of your serum. Final Thoughts: Find the Right Face Serum for Your Skin Having healthy and glowing skin involves using the right type of skin products and one such product is a face serum. The best face serum for women is the one which suits your skin type and meets your skin requirements, whether that's dryness, acne, dark spots, dullness, or signs of aging. Although there are no serums that work miracles overnight, regular use of a suitable product will have noticeable effects on your skin. As you explore the options in this guide, focus on ingredients that align with your skincare goals and introduce new products gradually. Using the serum together with the moisturizer and sunscreen will produce the best results for you. The more patience you have, the closer you will get to healthy, smoother, and naturally glowing skin.

title: Reprompt outperforms OpenAI, Claude, Gemini on hard places research tasks
summary: We benchmarked our places agent against GPT-5.5, o3-deep-research, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Claude Opus 4.8 on real-world human-verified places in Europe, North America, and Southeast Asia. The general agents do well on the easy web, but Reprompt outperforms on difficult geographies and tasks requiring deeper research.
body_text: Reprompt builds Deep Research Agents for business and places data. A common task is to check for the basic details of a place: is it still open, what are its hours, what's the phone number, what's the website. Our Agent harness is hand-built for the task and has over 40 tools at its disposal. But does it actually outperform frontier models from the AI labs, which also have tools and web access? Yes. To tune our agent, we constantly benchmark it against an updated dataset of hand-labeled places across the world. To benchmark against the AI labs, we sampled 158 real places across Southeast Asia, Europe, and North America. Five systems, same inputs, same JSON schema, same automatic scorer, human-verified answer key: OpenAI GPT-5.5 with native web search OpenAI Deep Research Gemini 3.5 Flash with Google Search Claude Opus 4.8 with web search Reprompt (our agent with its harness and tools) We scored against the fields that places teams care about most: permanent closures and opening hours. To make it a comparable benchmark, the labs were given our definition and schema for opening hours and closure. The only thing that changed was the agent harness and underlying LLM models. Permanent closures Reporting precision on whether a place is open or closed is a diluted metric- most places are open so most models will score above 95%. Instead we look at recall on closures: How many places were correctly identified as closed? From a dataset of over 800, we sampled 39 places that were human-confirmed to be permanently closed. Reprompt caught 36 of 39 closures, a 92% recall. System Closures caught Recall Reprompt 36 / 39 92% OpenAI Deep Research (o3) 25 / 39 64% Gemini 3.5 Flash 25 / 39 64% OpenAI GPT-5.5 23 / 39 59% Claude Opus 4.8 17 / 39 44% o3-deep-research is an interesting case. It spent a median of five minutes and ~75k tokens per place, and it still called 14 of the 39 closed businesses open. Not "unsure." Open. GPT 5.5 missed 41% of closures, Gemini 3.5 Flash missed 43%, and Claude Opus 4.8 missed 56%. For closures, the most common failure point is stopping early. The deep research models will find a plausible looking web result for a place and call it open instead of continuing to research. We know from experience that it only takes one credible closure source to render a place permanently closed For example, Razon's by Glenn in Ayala Malls closed, but it's still in a mall directory. That case fooled o3, GPT, Gemini, and Claude. GPT-5.5 said Cerería Ortega, a 131-year-old candle shop in Madrid, was open based on historical records; it closed in December 2024 and the closure was covered in the Madrid press. The reverse failure matters just as much: flagging live businesses as dead. Across the 137 truly open places our agent produced exactly one false "closed" — a McDonald's in Tacloban that was missing from the chain's JavaScript-rendered store locator. The only way to truly know a place is open is to call or visit, but deep web research is the next best thing. Opening hours Hours show a different issue: Fill rate is high across every system. For 80–92% of places, they return hours. The question is how often those hours are right. We scored 90 places with human-verified published hours. A schedule counts as correct if it matches the verified one on every day, within 15 minutes. System Answer rate Error rate when answered Reprompt 88% 16% OpenAI Deep Research (o3) 92% 29% OpenAI GPT-5.5 87% 21% Gemini 3.5 Flash 88% 28% Claude Opus 4.8 80% 32% o3 answers the most and verifies the least: wrong on 29% of the schedules it returns. Our agent is wrong on 16% which is the lowest, but still not a number we're satisfied with, because hours are genuinely hard: split shifts, seasonal schedules, a website that disagrees with the social profile it links to. A note on cost While cost and speed weren't a focus of this test, they're hard to ignore at global places scale (200M+ places). Reprompt is 5-10x cheaper than AI labs both due to fewer tokens spent, and cheaper search and page calls. Web search in particular is relatively expensive when used with the AI labs' models. Gemini Search Grounding costs $35/1000 requests and GPT's web search costs $10/1000 searches. ChatGPT Deep Research averaged over $2 per query and was overkill for this task. How we beat the AI lab models Given the same prompt and similar-class LLM model, we find that the Reprompt harness and toolset outperform the AI labs on difficult places tasks like opening hours and permanent closures. Reprompt especially shines in Southeast Asia and Europe where key information is more likely to be shared on Facebook, Instagram, or WhatsApp, and where aggregators are particularly outdated. And from the strict guardrails we've set, Reprompt is far less likely to mistake one entire place for another. Top error categories show how the general agents think: Wrong entity The closures that fooled the most systems were all outlets of healthy chains. The brand is alive and generating fresh which seems to trick the general agents into thinking the branch is too. Closure sources When a closure had press coverage, the general agents caught most of them. But when closure was cited in a single source such as a branch's listing webpage, the general agents were far more likely to mark it "open." We know from experience that it only takes one credible closure source to render a place permanently closed. Not citing enough sources In our source audit of 78 hours answers, GPT-5.5 cited one source or none for 71% of the schedules it returned; Reprompt answered from a single source on fewer than 8%, and typically cross-referenced three or more (official site, social profiles, aggregators as tie-breakers). Hallucinations The benchmark includes seven open places that verifiably publish no hours anywhere; the correct answer is null. Scored strictly that would drop GPT-5.5's hours precision to 70%. We find that generic agents, especially OpenAI's Deep Research are conditioned to produce an expansive, well-cited report. Intuitively, the labs want them to show something for all the tokens they've spent- "place not found" is an incredibly unsatisfying result. However, they often over-research to the point of pulling information about the wrong place or even hallucinating hours. Outlook We built Reprompt specifically for places tasks, and we've seen over the past 3 years where general agents fall short. We're pleased but not surprised that our harness and toolset outperform the AI labs. By design the Reprompt agent goes deeper into the web to validate information, ranks sources more effectively, and is more conservative and more accurate in its final answers. In short, we built Reprompt to be an exceptional places researcher and we're seeing that pay off in this test.
